rows.basis: Revenue of the Datacenter & Communications segment, 5,274,629,000 of 7,118,181,000 total; the Industrial segment is excluded. This is a data-center line, not an AI one: it includes telecom (communications) and non-AI datacom, and the company states no AI share. The MD&A gives the same segment figure ($5,275m, up 40%).

Revenue of the Datacenter & Communications segment (recast), 3,755,164,000 of 5,810,115,000; Industrial excluded. The MD&A ties growth to AI datacenter demand but also to telecom and data-center-interconnect growth, which this line includes; no AI share stated.

Revenue of the Datacenter & Communications segment (recast), 2,631,369,000 of 4,707,688,000; Industrial excluded. It includes telecom, which declined that year, and non-AI datacom. Quarterly 800G AI transceiver figures (over $100m in Q2 and almost $200m in Q3) and the guidance that AI would exceed 50% of datacom transceiver revenue do not give a full-year AI amount.

Words only: 'strong demand for transceivers in hyperscale datacenters and AI superclusters'. No Datacenter & Communications segment existed yet; the Networking and Photonic Solutions segments are not data-center lines.
The company expects 'continued strong growth ... throughout fiscal 2027 based on strong datacenter and communications demand'; no amount or AI share is given.

Capex of 1,102,909,000, up from 440,836,000, which the MD&A describes as capacity for the Datacenter and Communications markets, including indium phosphide in Sherman, Texas, and which the release ties to AI datacenter scaling. No amount or share is split out, so the total is not attributed. The seller-side signal is Datacenter & Communications revenue of 5,274,629,000.
Capex of 440,836,000. The only link is a forward statement from fiscal 2024 about expanding four wafer fabs for 800G, 1.6T and 3.2T datacom lasers. No amount is split out.
A multi-year agreement with NVIDIA (2 Mar 2026) covers optics manufacturing capacity and R&D 'to enable next-generation AI infrastructure'. No capex amount is stated.
The MD&A says internal R&D includes 'significant investments in datacom transceivers for AI' among several other programs. No amount is given, and the pack has no opex value.
The NVIDIA strategic agreement includes research and development for next-generation AI infrastructure optics. No amount is stated.
